proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(S\in\mathcal I\), put \(U=V\setminus S\) and \(O=X\setminus S\), and set \(A=Q^{-1}\).  The inclusion \(\varnothing\in\mathcal I\) and Assumption \(\texttt{ass:regime-solvability}\) give \(\det Q\ne0\), while the same assumption at \(S\) gives \(\det Q_{U,U}\ne0\).  Empty matrices have determinant one throughout.  Block elimination in the order \((S,U)\) gives
\[
 \det Q=\det(Q_{U,U})
 \det\!\left(Q_{S,S}-Q_{S,U}Q_{U,U}^{-1}Q_{U,S}\right)
\]
and the block-inverse identity gives
\[
 A_{S,S}=\left(Q_{S,S}-Q_{S,U}Q_{U,U}^{-1}Q_{U,S}\right)^{-1}.
\]
Because \(S\subseteq X\), \(C_{S,S}=A_{S,S}\).  Therefore
\[
 \det(C_{S,S})=\frac{\det(Q_{U,U})}{\det Q}\ne0.                    \tag{1}
\]

The \((U,S)\) block of \(QA=I_N\) is
\[
 Q_{U,U}A_{U,S}+Q_{U,S}A_{S,S}=0.
\]
Since \(Q_{U,S}=-B_{U,S}\), equation (1) yields
\[
 T_S(C)=C_{O,S}C_{S,S}^{-1}
       =\bigl[Q_{U,U}^{-1}B_{U,S}\bigr]_{O,:}.                       \tag{2}
\]
The \((U,U)\) block of \(QA=I_N\) similarly gives
\[
 A_{U,U}-Q_{U,U}^{-1}B_{U,S}A_{S,U}=Q_{U,U}^{-1}.                    \tag{3}
\]
By Definition \(\texttt{def:intervention-response-maps}\), equations (2)--(3) say that \(R_S(C)\) has zero columns on \(S\) and
\[
 R_S(C)_{:,U}=(Q_{U,U}^{-1})_{O,U}.                                  \tag{4}
\]

Assumption \(\texttt{ass:perfect-intervention}\) replaces precisely the equations in \(S\).  Hence the remaining structural equations are
\[
 Q_{U,U}V_U=\varepsilon_U+B_{U,S}x.
\]
Equations (2) and (4) imply, on the structural probability space,
\[
 X_O^{\operatorname{do}(X_S=x)}=R_S(C)\varepsilon+T_S(C)x.
\]
Taking laws proves
\[
 K_S^{B,\varepsilon}(x)
 =\mathcal L\bigl(R_S(C)\varepsilon+T_S(C)x\bigr).                   \tag{5}
\]
In the observational regime \(X=C\varepsilon\), so the definition of \(R_S\) gives the samplewise identity
\[
 R_S(C)\varepsilon=X_O-T_S(C)X_S.                                   \tag{6}
\]
Thus the observational law determines the law on the right of (6), and (5) determines every response kernel once the finite collection of matrices \(T_S(C)\) is supplied.  Finally, if \(C_{:,i}=0\), then both \(C_{O,i}\) and \(C_{S,i}\) vanish, whence \(R_S(C)_{:,i}=0\) for every \(S\).  Thus an observationally invisible source stays invisible under every allowed intervention.  No expectation, moment, centering, positivity, boundary, or limiting argument is used.  The identities also cover \(S=\varnothing\), \(O=\varnothing\), and zero residual columns under the stated empty-matrix conventions.

We first prove directed containment.  Assume
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H),          \tag{12}
\]
and fix \(C\in\mathcal D_G\).  The already established Theorem \(\texttt{thm:exact-mixing-realization}\) supplies an exact-support \(G\)-matrix \(Q\) satisfying every required principal invertibility condition and having \((Q^{-1})_{X,:}=C\).  Put on this matrix the diagnostic independent finite-support source vector supplied by Lemma \(\texttt{lem:diagnostic-mixture-rigidity}\).  Its coordinates are nonconstant and non-Gaussian, so Definition \(\texttt{def:exact-support-model-class}\) makes this an admissible mechanism; no centering or moment condition is required.

By (12), the resulting entire response-kernel tuple is generated by an admissible \(H\)-mechanism.  Let \(D\) be its observed mixing matrix.  The backward implication of exact mixing realization gives \(D\in\mathcal D_H\).  Equality of the observational components is
\[
 \mathcal L(C\varepsilon)=\mathcal L(D\eta).
\]
Diagnostic rigidity therefore supplies a surjection \(f:U_C\twoheadrightarrow U_D\) and nonzero \(a_i\) such that
\[
 C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)},\qquad i\in U_C.                              \tag{13}
\]

Fix \(S\in\mathcal I\).  By Lemma \(\texttt{lem:intervention-pushforward}\), equality of the two kernels says
\[
 \mathcal L\bigl(R_S(C)\varepsilon+T_S(C)x\bigr)
 =\mathcal L\bigl(R_S(D)\eta+T_S(D)x\bigr)
 \quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^S.                              \tag{14}
\]
At \(x=0\), the residual laws in (14) equal a common probability measure \(\mu_S\).  Thus for every \(x\), translation of \(\mu_S\) by \(T_S(C)x\) equals translation by \(T_S(D)x\).  Lemma \(\texttt{lem:probability-translation-rigidity}\) gives
\[
 (T_S(C)-T_S(D))x=0\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^S,
\]
and hence \(T_S(C)=T_S(D)\).  This also covers an empty domain or codomain.  We have verified every clause of \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\).

Conversely, assume \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\), and take an arbitrary admissible \(G\)-mechanism with observed mixing matrix \(C\) and independent nonconstant non-Gaussian source vector \(\varepsilon\).  Exact mixing realization places \(C\) in \(\mathcal D_G\).  Choose a cover witness \((D,f,a)\).  The same theorem constructs an exact-support, regime-solvable \(H\)-matrix with observed mixing \(D\).  For \(j\in U_D\), define once and for all
\[
 \eta_j=\sum_{i:f(i)=j}a_i\varepsilon_i.                              \tag{15}
\]
Disjoint, nonempty fibers make these variables mutually independent.  The support argument and L\'evy--Cram\'er argument in the proof of Lemma \(\texttt{lem:finite-mixture-containment-unrestricted}\) show that each is nonconstant and non-Gaussian.  Choose arbitrary independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources on the invisible columns, independent of (15).  Thus this is one admissible \(H\)-source tuple, common to all regimes.  Equation (13), now as a cover clause, gives the samplewise equality \(C\varepsilon=D\eta\).

For every \(S\in\mathcal I\) and \(i\in U_C\), proportionality of the full observed columns and equality of response matrices imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_S(C)_{:,i}
 &=C_{X\setminus S,i}-T_S(C)C_{S,i}\\
 &=a_i\bigl(D_{X\setminus S,f(i)}-T_S(D)D_{S,f(i)}\bigr)\\
 &=a_iR_S(D)_{:,f(i)}.                                                 \tag{16}
 \end{aligned}
\]
If \(i\notin U_C\), its residual column is zero by the intervention-pushforward lemma; surjectivity ensures that every visible \(D\)-column appears in (15).  Summing (16) over the source fibers yields
\[
 R_S(C)\varepsilon=R_S(D)\eta.
\]
Together with \(T_S(C)=T_S(D)\), the pushforward identity proves equality of the two kernels for every \(x\), simultaneously for every \(S\).  Hence the whole tuple belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)\), proving the reverse implication.

We have established
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H).
\]
Applying this equivalence in both directions proves the equality criterion.  Every zero pattern, rank incidence, and punctured exact-support condition is retained in \(\mathcal D_G\) and \(\mathcal D_H\); no generic, closure, boundary, or limiting argument occurs.

We construct the advertised formula before invoking elimination.  A rank equality for a matrix with at most \(N\) rows and columns is a finite disjunction over its possible rank: a chosen pivot minor is nonzero and every larger minor vanishes.  Applying this to every local system in Definition \(\texttt{def:exact-mixing-domain}\), Gaussian elimination on a chosen pivot chart writes an affine base point and a basis of the direction space of each fiber \(\mathcal A_j(C)\) as rational functions of \(C\).  The only denominators are the selected nonzero minors.  Adjoining the base point gives a rational spanning family for \(W_j(C)\).  Therefore each Hall--Rado inequality is the finite minor condition
\[
 \operatorname{rank}[W_j(C):j\in J]\geq |J|,
 \qquad J\subseteq L.
\]
Clearing the chart denominators does not change the condition on a chart.  The punctured-coordinate requirements and intervention principal minors are likewise Boolean combinations of polynomial equalities and strict inequalities.  Theorem \(\texttt{thm:exact-mixing-realization}\) proves that the resulting quantifier-free formula \(\operatorname{Dom}_G(C)\) defines exactly \(\mathcal D_G\), including all singular and lower-dimensional chart intersections.

For visible sets \(U,W\subseteq V\) and a surjection \(f:U\twoheadrightarrow W\), introduce at most \(N\) scalars \(a_i\) and impose
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &C_{:,i}=0\Longleftrightarrow i\notin U,
 &&D_{:,j}=0\Longleftrightarrow j\notin W,\\
 &a_i\ne0,
 &&C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}\quad(i\in U).                                \tag{17}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Column nonzeroness is the strict polynomial inequality \(\sum_{r\in X}C_{ri}^2>0\).  On the domain charts, response equality is polynomialized without an inverse as
\[
 C_{O,S}\operatorname{adj}(C_{S,S})\det(D_{S,S})
 =D_{O,S}\operatorname{adj}(D_{S,S})\det(C_{S,S}),
 \qquad O=X\setminus S.                                                \tag{18}
\]
Both determinants are nonzero on the domain, so (18) is equivalent to \(T_S(C)=T_S(D)\).

Let \(\Theta_f(C,D,a)\) conjoin \(\operatorname{Dom}_H(D)\), (17), and (18) for all \(S\in\mathcal I\).  The directed compiler decides
\[
 \forall C\in\mathbb R^{n\times N}\;
 \left[
 \operatorname{Dom}_G(C)\Longrightarrow
 \bigvee_{U,W,f}\exists D\in\mathbb R^{n\times N}
 \exists a\in\mathbb R^U\;\Theta_f(C,D,a)
 \right].                                                              \tag{19}
\]
By Definition \(\texttt{def:directed-chart-cover}\), (19) is precisely \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\); Theorem \(\texttt{thm:coupled-equivalence}\) then makes it equivalent to directed response-kernel containment.  The source-distribution quantifier has already been eliminated by Theorem \(\texttt{thm:unrestricted-source-partition-containment}\), and the structural matrix \(B\) by exact mixing realization.  Thus real-algebraic elimination is applied to the new finite chart representation, not to the original mechanism-existence problem.

We verify the stated size bounds.  Every local or pivot matrix has at most \(N\) rows and columns and hence at most \(2^{2N}\) minors.  Choosing pivot data for at most \(N\) local systems produces at most \(2^{2N^2}\) joint charts.  A concatenated Hall matrix has at most \(N\) rows and \(N^2\) columns and fewer than \(2^{N+N^2}\) minors.  The \(2^\ell\) Hall subfamilies, \(q\) intervention blocks, and zero-pattern clauses fit within \((q+N+1)2^{4N^2}\) additional recorded atoms.  Finally, the number of pairs of visible subsets and partial source maps is at most
\[
 2^{2N}(N+1)^N\leq2^{3N^2}\qquad(N\geq2).
\]
Sharing repeated atoms gives the conservative total
\[
 s=(q+N+1)2^{8N^2}.
\]
Pivot denominators are minors of degree at most \(N\); a Hall minor uses at most \(N\) rational entries, and clearing at most \(N\) denominators leaves degree below \(d=4N^3\).  Equations (17)--(18) have smaller degree.  Expanding the fewer than \(2^{8N^2}\) recorded determinant atoms by the Leibniz formula bounds the integer coefficient bit length by
\[
 \tau=(\lambda+1)2^{8N^2}.
\]
These bounds include empty blocks and zero signs.

Formula (19) has two real quantifier blocks, of sizes at most \(p=nN\) and \(p+N\).  Lemma \(\texttt{lem:effective-real-quantifier-elimination}\) therefore gives
\[
 (\tau+1)^2(s+1)^{(p+1)(p+N+1)+1}
 (d+1)^{c_{\mathrm{qe}}(p+1)(p+N+1)}
 =\mathsf B(N,q,\lambda)
\]
bit operations after the one advertised enlargement of the absolute constant.  Its sign conditions and algebraic sample encodings form a finite certificate.  Zero signs are retained, so the certificate includes forced zeros, nullification, Hall--Rado failures, and lower-dimensional cells.  Running the decision in both directions proves the comparison bound.

There are \(2^{N(N-1)}\) labeled loopless digraphs.  For each candidate, perform the two directed decisions.  To quotient only latent relabeling, compute the least adjacency encoding under the \(\ell!\) simultaneous row-and-column permutations fixing every observed label, at cost at most \(\ell!N^2\).  This proves the enumeration bound, termination, and completeness, with no centering or moment premise.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(\mu\) be a Borel probability measure on \(\mathbb R^k\), where \(k\geq0\), and let \(h\in\mathbb R^k\).  If translation by \(h\) preserves \(\mu\), then \(h=0\).  Consequently, if \(\mathcal L(Z+u)=\mathcal L(Z+v)\) for an \(\mathbb R^k\)-valued random vector \(Z\), then \(u=v\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The assertion is immediate for \(k=0\).  Suppose \(k>0\) and, toward a contradiction, \(h
e0\).  Push \(\mu\) forward by the linear functional \(z\mapsto h^{\mathsf T}z/\lVert hVert\).  The resulting probability measure \(
u\) on \(\mathbb R\) is invariant under translation by \(r=\lVert hVert>0\).  The half-open Borel intervals
\[
 I_m=[mr,(m+1)r),\qquad m\in\mathbb Z,
\]
are pairwise disjoint, cover \(\mathbb R\), and all have the same \(
u\)-mass \(c\).  If \(c>0\), countable additivity gives \(
u(\mathbb R)=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}c=\infty\); if \(c=0\), it gives \(
u(\mathbb R)=0\).  Both conclusions contradict \(
u(\mathbb R)=1\).  Hence \(h=0\).  For the consequence, translating \(\mathcal L(Z+u)=\mathcal L(Z+v)\) by \(-v\) shows that \(\mathcal L(Z)\) is invariant under translation by \(u-v\), so the first part gives \(u=v\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(r,m\geq0\), let \(p_i\in(0,1)\) for \(1\leq i\leq r\), and let \(F_1,\ldots,F_m\) be nonzero Laurent polynomials in \(z_1,\ldots,z_r\) with nonnegative real coefficients.  If
\[
 \prod_{j=1}^m F_j(z)=c z^\gamma
 \prod_{i=1}^r\bigl((1-p_i)+p_i z_i\bigr)
\]
for \(c>0\) and \(\gamma\in\mathbb Z^r\), then there is a partition \((I_j)_{j=1}^m\) of \(\{1,\ldots,r\}\), positive constants \(c_j\), and \(\gamma_j\in\mathbb Z^r\) such that
\[
 F_j(z)=c_jz^{\gamma_j}\prod_{i\in I_j}
 \bigl((1-p_i)+p_i z_i\bigr)
\]
for every \(j\).  If every \(F_j\) has at least two monomials, then every \(I_j\) is nonempty.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(L_i(z_i)=(1-p_i)+p_i z_i\).  Multiplying each \(F_j\) by a Laurent monomial, and compensating in \(z^\gamma\), reduces to ordinary polynomials not divisible by any coordinate monomial.  We prove directly that every \(L_i\) is prime in the multivariate polynomial ring.  Regard that ring as \(A[z_i]\), where \(A\) is the real polynomial ring in the other variables.  The ring \(A\) is an integral domain because the leading monomial of a product of two nonzero polynomials has nonzero coefficient.  Division by the linear polynomial \(L_i\), whose leading coefficient \(p_i\) is a nonzero real unit, shows that
\[
 L_i\mid P \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 P\bigl(z_i=-(1-p_i)/p_i\bigr)=0.
\]
If \(L_i\mid P Q\), evaluation at that root gives a product equal to zero in the integral domain \(A\), so \(L_i\mid P\) or \(L_i\mid Q\).  Thus \(L_i\) is prime.  Two different \(L_i\)'s are not associates because they involve different variables.

Apply this prime-divisibility argument successively to the displayed product identity.  Each prime \(L_i\) divides at least one factor \(F_j\), and it cannot divide two factors because their product would then have degree at least two in \(z_i\), whereas the right side has degree one in \(z_i\) after removal of its Laurent monomial unit.  Thus each \(L_i\) divides exactly one \(F_j\).  After removing all such factors, the remaining factors multiply to a unit in the Laurent ring.  A Laurent polynomial is a unit only if it is a nonzero constant times a monomial: after shifting it to an ordinary polynomial with nonzero constant term, a product equal to one forces both factors to have degree zero in every variable.  Hence each remaining factor is \(c_jz^{\gamma_j}\), and the sets of allocated indices form the required partition.  Evaluating the identity at \(z_1=\cdots=z_r=1\) and using the nonnegative, nonzero coefficients makes every \(c_j\) positive.  Finally, a factor with \(I_j=\varnothing\) has exactly one monomial, so the last assertion follows.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(k,p\geq0\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{k\times p}\).  There is a vector \(\xi^A\) of mutually independent, nonconstant, non-Gaussian, finite-support real random variables such that, for every \(q\geq0\), every \(D\in\mathbb R^{k\times q}\), and every vector \(\eta\) of mutually independent nonconstant real random variables, the equality \(\mathcal L(A\xi^A)=\mathcal L(D\eta)\) implies the existence of a surjection \(f:U_A\twoheadrightarrow U_D\) and nonzero scalars \(a_i\), \(i\in U_A\), satisfying \(A_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}\).  If the coordinates of \(\eta\) are also non-Gaussian, this conclusion remains unchanged.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(F\) be the subfield of \(\mathbb R\) generated by the finitely many entries of \(A\); it is countable.  Put \(U=U_A\).  Choose positive numbers \((r_i)_{i\in U}\) algebraically independent over \(F\).  Such a finite family exists recursively because the elements algebraic over a countable field form a countable set, whereas every nonempty real interval is uncountable.  Set \(h_i=r_iA_{:,i}\).  If \(\sum_{i\in U}m_i h_i=0\) for integers \(m_i\), every coordinate gives a polynomial relation over \(F\) among the \(r_i\)'s.  Algebraic independence implies \(m_iA_{vi}=0\) for every \(v,i\), and the nonzeroness of column \(i\) gives \(m_i=0\).  Hence
\[
 \Lambda=\bigoplus_{i\in U}\mathbb Z h_i                                      \tag{7}
\]
is a free abelian group on the displayed generators.

Choose \(p_i\in(0,1)\), take independent \(Z_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_i)\), and put \(\xi_i^A=r_iZ_i\) for \(i\in U\).  Give the zero columns independent nonconstant Bernoulli coordinates as well.  These coordinates have finite support and are non-Gaussian.  By (7), the law of \(A\xi^A\) has the \(2^{|U|}\) distinct support points
\[
 \left\{\sum_{i\in U}z_i h_i:z_i\in\{0,1\}\right\}.                         \tag{8}
\]

Suppose \(\mathcal L(A\xi^A)=\mathcal L(D\eta)\), and write \(Y_j=D_{:,j}\eta_j\) for \(j\in U_D\).  The support of a convolution contains the Minkowski sum of the supports: if one chooses a support point from each independent summand, every product neighborhood has positive probability and its sum is a neighborhood of the summed point.  Since (8) is finite, fixing support points of all but one \(Y_j\) shows that each \(Y_j\) has finite support.  Moreover, \(Y_j\) is nonconstant because \(D_{:,j}\ne0\) and \(\eta_j\) is nonconstant.

Choose \(y_j^0\in\operatorname{supp}(Y_j)\).  If \(y\in\operatorname{supp}(Y_j)\), hold all other selected support points fixed and compare the two resulting sums.  Both belong to (8), so \(y-y_j^0\in\Lambda\).  Freeness in (7) gives a unique vector \(\nu_j(y)\in\mathbb Z^U\) with
\[
 y-y_j^0=\sum_{i\in U}\nu_j(y)_i h_i.
\]
Define the finite Laurent polynomial
\[
 F_j(z)=\sum_{y\in\operatorname{supp}(Y_j)}
          \Pr(Y_j=y)z^{\nu_j(y)}.
\]
Independence and equality of the two laws imply coefficient by coefficient, using the injective map from exponent vectors to \(\Lambda\), that
\[
 \prod_{j\in U_D}F_j(z)
 =c z^\gamma\prod_{i\in U}\bigl((1-p_i)+p_i z_i\bigr)                         \tag{9}
\]
for a positive \(c\) and a Laurent monomial \(z^\gamma\).  The proved Laurent-factorization lemma partitions \(U\) into nonempty sets \((I_j)_{j\in U_D}\).  They are nonempty because each \(Y_j\), and hence each \(F_j\), is nonconstant.  If \(i\in I_j\), the product form of \(F_j\) has two support exponents differing by the \(i\)-th coordinate vector.  Thus two support points of \(Y_j\) differ by \(h_i\).  Both points lie on the line \(\mathbb R D_{:,j}\), so
\[
 A_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,j}
\]
for some \(a_i\ne0\).  Setting \(f(i)=j\) for \(i\in I_j\) gives the asserted surjection.

If \(U=\varnothing\), the left side is constant.  The same support argument forces every \(Y_j\) to be constant, which contradicts \(j\in U_D\); hence \(U_D=\varnothing\) and the empty map is the required surjection.  The argument imposed no Gaussianity condition on \(\eta\), so it applies in particular when its coordinates are non-Gaussian.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(k,p,q\) be nonnegative integers and let \(A\in\mathbb R^{k\times p}\) and \(D\in\mathbb R^{k\times q}\).  Write \(U_A\) and \(U_D\) for their sets of nonzero columns, and let \(\mathscr L(A)\) be the set of laws of \(A\xi\) as the coordinates of \(\xi\) range independently over all nonconstant, non-Gaussian real laws, without centering or moment restrictions.  Then \(\mathscr L(A)\subseteq\mathscr L(D)\) if and only if there are a surjection \(f:U_A\twoheadrightarrow U_D\) and nonzero real numbers \(a_i\), \(i\in U_A\), such that \(A_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}\) for every \(i\in U_A\).  This includes \(k=0\) and zero columns.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Assume first that \(\mathscr L(A)\subseteq\mathscr L(D)\).  Apply containment to the diagnostic source vector \(\xi^A\) from Lemma \(\texttt{lem:diagnostic-mixture-rigidity}\).  Its coordinates are legal for \(\mathscr L(A)\), so there is a legal independent nonconstant non-Gaussian vector \(\eta\) with
\[
 \mathcal L(A\xi^A)=\mathcal L(D\eta).
\]
Diagnostic rigidity supplies the required surjection and nonzero proportionality scalars.

Conversely, suppose \(f\) and \((a_i)\) exist, and take an arbitrary legal source vector \(\xi\) for \(A\).  For \(j\in U_D\), define
\[
 \eta_j=\sum_{i:f(i)=j}a_i\xi_i.                                      \tag{10}
\]
The fibers of the surjection are disjoint and nonempty, so the variables in (10) are mutually independent.  Each summand in (10) is nonconstant and non-Gaussian.  The sum cannot be constant: the support of a sum of independent random variables contains the sum of their supports, so a singleton support for the sum would force every summand support to be a singleton.  The sum also cannot be Gaussian.  If it were a nondegenerate Gaussian, Lemma \(\texttt{lem:levy-cramer-decomposition}\) would force every nonconstant summand to be Gaussian, a contradiction.  Thus every \(\eta_j\) in (10) is nonconstant and non-Gaussian.  Give each invisible column \(j\notin U_D\) an arbitrary independent Bernoulli source, independent also of (10).  Then
\[
 D\eta
 =\sum_{j\in U_D}D_{:,j}\sum_{i:f(i)=j}a_i\xi_i
 =\sum_{i\in U_A}A_{:,i}\xi_i
 =A\xi.                                                               \tag{11}
\]
Thus every law in \(\mathscr L(A)\) belongs to \(\mathscr L(D)\).  The support argument also covers \(k=0\), and empty visible sets use the unique empty surjection.  No centering, moment, boundary, or limit condition enters either direction.

added_lemmas.statement: For fixed \(C\in\mathcal D_G\) and \(D\in\mathcal D_H\), every observable mixture law generated from \(C\) by arbitrary independent nonconstant non-Gaussian real sources, without centering or moment restrictions, is generated from \(D\) if and only if there exist a surjection \(f:U_C\twoheadrightarrow U_D\) and nonzero scalars \(a_i\) with \(C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}\) for all \(i\in U_C\).  Necessity is certified by one admissible Bernoulli diagnostic in its original free jump lattice, and sufficiency merges sources along the fibers of \(f\) while preserving nonconstancy and non-Gaussianity.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For a fixed mixing matrix \(A\), let \(\mathscr L(A)\) have the meaning in Lemma \(\texttt{lem:finite-mixture-containment-unrestricted}\).  With \(A=C\), the assertion that every observable mixture law generated from \(C\) is generated from \(D\) is exactly \(\mathscr L(C)\subseteq\mathscr L(D)\).  That lemma proves
\[
 \mathscr L(C)\subseteq\mathscr L(D)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists f:U_C\twoheadrightarrow U_D\;
 \exists(a_i)_{i\in U_C}\in(\mathbb R\setminus\{0\})^{U_C};
 \forall i\in U_C:\ C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}.
\]
Its necessity invokes the explicitly constructed Bernoulli diagnostic of Lemma \(\texttt{lem:diagnostic-mixture-rigidity}\), whose jump generators are free in their original lattice.  Its sufficiency uses the fiber sums in equation (10), with nonconstancy proved by support and non-Gaussianity by Lemma \(\texttt{lem:levy-cramer-decomposition}\).  Zero columns contribute nothing and receive arbitrary legal independent sources.  This proves both directions, including invisible columns, irreversible source merging, and source-law symmetries, without a centering or moment assumption.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every loopless graph \(G\),
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G)
 =\bigcup_{F:\,E(F)\subseteq E(G)}\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(F).          \tag{20}
\]
For every loopless graph pair \(G,H\),
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G)
 \subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(H)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G,H).                       \tag{21}
\]
Consequently the two zero-allowed joint response-kernel model sets are equal if and only if both directed downward-closed cover relations hold.  This is a finite union over exact-support strata and retains one common coefficient matrix and one common source-law tuple across all regimes.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Take a mechanism in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G)\), and let \(F\) be the unique loopless graph with edge set \(E(F)=\operatorname{supp}(B)\).  Then \(E(F)\subseteq E(G)\); all regime-solvability, source, and surgical-intervention conditions are unchanged, so the mechanism belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathcal I}(F)\).  This proves the left-to-right inclusion in (20).  Conversely, if a mechanism belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathcal I}(F)\) for some \(E(F)\subseteq E(G)\), then its exact support is contained in \(E(G)\), so it belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G)\).  This proves (20).  The union is finite because a loopless graph has at most \(N(N-1)\) possible edges.

We prove (21).  Assume first the set containment and fix \(F\subseteq G\) and \(C\in\mathcal D_F\).  Exact mixing realization produces an exact-support, regime-solvable matrix on \(F\) with observed mixing \(C\).  Equip it with the diagnostic sources from Lemma \(\texttt{lem:diagnostic-mixture-rigidity}\).  Its response-kernel tuple lies in \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G)\), hence in \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(H)\).  Choose a realizing zero-allowed \(H\)-mechanism, let \(K\) be its exact structural support, and let \(D\) be its observed mixing matrix.  Then \(E(K)\subseteq E(H)\), and exact mixing realization gives \(D\in\mathcal D_K\).

Equality of the observational kernels and diagnostic rigidity give a surjection \(f:U_C\twoheadrightarrow U_D\) and nonzero \(a_i\) satisfying \(C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}\).  For every \(S\), the pushforward lemma writes the equal kernels as translates of their equal residual law at \(x=0\).  Translation rigidity therefore gives \(T_S(C)=T_S(D)\), exactly as in equations (14).  Thus \((K,D,f,a)\) witnesses \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G,H)\).

Conversely, assume the downward-closed cover and take any zero-allowed \(G\)-mechanism.  Let \(F\subseteq G\) be its exact support and \(C\in\mathcal D_F\) its observed mixing matrix.  A cover witness supplies \(K\subseteq H\), \(D\in\mathcal D_K\), \(f\), and \(a\).  Exact mixing realization constructs the corresponding exact-support matrix on \(K\).  Define its visible sources by the single common grouping
\[
 \eta_j=\sum_{i:f(i)=j}a_i\varepsilon_i,\qquad j\in U_D,            \tag{22}
\]
and choose arbitrary legal independent sources on invisible columns.  As proved in unrestricted finite-mixture containment, (22) gives independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources and \(C\varepsilon=D\eta\).  Proportionality and simultaneous response equality give equation (16) for every \(S\), hence
\[
 R_S(C)\varepsilon+T_S(C)x
 =R_S(D)\eta+T_S(D)x
\]
samplewise for all \(S\) and \(x\).  The pushforward lemma shows that the entire joint tuple is realized by this one \(K\)-mechanism and this one source tuple.  Because \(K\subseteq H\), it lies in \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(H)\).  This proves the reverse implication in (21).  Applying (21) in both directions proves the equality criterion.  In particular, no monotone transfer of exact-support equality was assumed: the proof explicitly quantifies over every exact stratum \(F\subseteq G\), allows the target stratum \(K\subseteq H\) to depend on \(C\), and constructs the common multi-regime realization.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(q=|\mathcal I|\), \(p=nN\), \(R_N=2^{N(N-1)}\), and retain \(s=(q+N+1)2^{8N^2}\), \(d=4N^3\), and \(\tau=(\lambda+1)2^{8N^2}\) from Theorem \(\texttt{thm:effective-population-compiler}\).  Put \(s_{\leq}=R_Ns\) and
\[
 \mathsf B_{\leq}(N,q,\lambda)
 =R_N(\tau+1)^2(s_{\leq}+1)^{(p+1)(p+N+1)+1}
 (d+1)^{c_{\mathrm{qe}}(p+1)(p+N+1)}.                                 \tag{23}
\]
There is a terminating exact compiler deciding \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G,H)\) within \(\mathsf B_{\leq}(N,q,\lambda)\) bit operations and zero-allowed equivalence within \(2\mathsf B_{\leq}(N,q,\lambda)\) bit operations.  It enumerates the zero-allowed equivalence class of \(G\) modulo latent relabeling within
\[
 R_N\bigl(2\mathsf B_{\leq}(N,q,\lambda)+\ell!N^2\bigr)               \tag{24}
\]
bit operations, apart from fixed linear-time encoding overhead.  Its output is a finite sign-cell certificate and contains neither a structural-coefficient quantifier nor a source-law quantifier.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For each spanning subgraph \(F\subseteq G\), reuse the exact compiler's quantifier-free formula \(\operatorname{Dom}_F(C)\).  For each \(K\subseteq H\), reuse its witness formula \(\Theta_{K,f}(C,D,a)\), with the domain clause changed only from \(\operatorname{Dom}_H(D)\) to \(\operatorname{Dom}_K(D)\).  The clause required for this fixed \(F\) is
\[
 \forall C\;\left[
 \operatorname{Dom}_F(C)\Longrightarrow
 \exists(D,a)\bigvee_{K\subseteq H}\bigvee_{U,W,f}
 \Theta_{K,f}(C,D,a)
 \right].                                                              \tag{25}
\]
The finite disjunction may be placed inside the one existential block because every disjunct uses the same padded \(D\)-matrix and at most \(N\) padded scalar variables.  By Definition \(\texttt{def:downward-closed-cover}\), the conjunction of (25) over \(F\subseteq G\) is exactly \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G,H)\).  Theorem \(\texttt{thm:zero-allowed-coupled-equivalence}\) proves that its truth is equivalent to zero-allowed law-set containment.

There are at most \(R_N\) choices of \(F\) and at most \(R_N\) choices of \(K\).  For a fixed \(F\), the added \(K\)-disjunction multiplies the exact compiler's number of recorded polynomial atoms by at most \(R_N\), so it uses at most \(s_{\leq}=R_Ns\) atoms.  It introduces no new real variable, and its polynomials are copied from the exact charts; their degree remains at most \(d\) and their coefficient bit length at most \(\tau\).  Thus Lemma \(\texttt{lem:effective-real-quantifier-elimination}\) decides one formula (25) within
\[
 (\tau+1)^2(s_{\leq}+1)^{(p+1)(p+N+1)+1}
 (d+1)^{c_{\mathrm{qe}}(p+1)(p+N+1)}
\]
bit operations.  Running it for all at most \(R_N\) source strata gives (23).  The elimination output retains zero sign conditions and algebraic sample encodings, so concatenating the at most \(R_N\) certificates gives a finite certificate for the conjunction, including every lower-dimensional incidence.

Two directed runs decide equality.  Finally enumerate the \(R_N\) labeled loopless candidate graphs and, for each accepted candidate, canonicalize under the \(\ell!\) latent-label permutations at cost at most \(\ell!N^2\).  This proves (24).  Exact mixing realization removed \(B\), unrestricted source-partition containment removed all source laws, and only the explicitly displayed mixing, scaling, and finite chart variables remain in (25).  Hence the algorithm terminates with the claimed representation and is not black-box elimination of the original structural-existence formula.

proposed.name: Directed downward-closed coupled cover
proposed.construction: \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G,H)\) holds exactly when, for every loopless spanning subgraph \(F\) with \(E(F)\subseteq E(G)\) and every \(C\in\mathcal D_F\), there exist a loopless spanning subgraph \(K\) with \(E(K)\subseteq E(H)\), a matrix \(D\in\mathcal D_K\), a surjection \(f:U_C\twoheadrightarrow U_D\), and nonzero scalars \((a_i)_{i\in U_C}\) such that \(C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}\) for every \(i\in U_C\) and \(T_S(C)=T_S(D)\) for every \(S\in\mathcal I\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This definition exposes the finite source-stratum and target-stratum disjunction required for zero-allowed containment instead of assuming monotone transfer from exact-support equality.

proposed.statement: For every \(S\in\mathcal I\) and every mechanism in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathcal I}(G)\), \(\det(C_{S,S})\ne0\) and \(K_S^{B,\varepsilon}(x)=\mathcal L(R_S(C)\varepsilon+T_S(C)x)\). Moreover, \(R_S(C)\varepsilon=X_{X\setminus S}-T_S(C)X_S\) observationally. Hence the observational law together with \(\{T_S(C):S\in\mathcal I\}\) determines the entire joint tuple of affine response kernels, including every cancellation and every observationally invisible source.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof is purely algebraic and no longer uses source centering; the dependency metadata must match the broadened population class.
The centered finite-second-moment version is obsolete; the replacement proves the same exact partition criterion for the full uncentered, moment-unrestricted population source class.
The old source theorem inherited unnecessary centering and moment restrictions; the replacement is the load-bearing theorem for the broadened exact and zero-allowed classes.

proposed.statement: For every finite \(X\), fixed \(\ell\), finite \(\mathcal I\ni\varnothing\), and loopless graph pair \(G,H\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\). Consequently, \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)=\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)\) if and only if both \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\) and \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(H,G)\) hold. This criterion is exact on lower-dimensional rank, cancellation, nullification, invisible-source, and source-symmetry strata, and it is a finite graph-generated compatibility representation rather than the original structural-existence formula.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The claim is unchanged, but its proof now uses diagnostic-mixture rigidity and translation rigidity rather than moments and its dependency spine must point to the unrestricted source theorem.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper gives a sound-and-complete finite criterion for equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel sets in latent linear non-Gaussian feedback models. The exact-support theorem combines exact affine and Hall--Rado realization, a Bernoulli-diagnostic source-partition theorem, and simultaneous response matrices for one common mechanism. A new downward-closure theorem proves \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G)=\bigcup_{F\subseteq G}\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(F)\) and characterizes the zero-allowed class by a finite exact-stratum cover, while explicit sign-cell compilers decide both versions with size-dependent bit bounds. Centering and moments are absent from the population equivalence theory and remain local to the finite-variance witness and statistical subclass.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. characterize observational distributional equivalence for the zero-allowed LiNG class; existing results do not characterize equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel sets or the additional requirement that one mechanism and source tuple realize all regimes. Graphical intervention equivalence for latent acyclic models and second-order experiment-design recovery address different objects and do not supply this cyclic full-law common-mechanism criterion.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a finite coupled invariant that retains exact structural completion, lower-dimensional cancellations, invisible or merged independent sources, principal intervention responses, and common-mechanism gluing. Its downward closure must compare every exact support stratum of the source graph against a finite disjunction of exact support strata of the target graph; exact-support equality alone does not transfer monotonically.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the exact-stratum criterion using graph-generated affine and rank charts, eliminates arbitrary source laws with an admissible Bernoulli diagnostic and Laurent factorization, and identifies response slopes by rigidity of probability laws under nonzero translation. It then proves the finite union formula and downward-closed cover criterion for zero-allowed supports and compiles both relations by effective sign-condition elimination with explicit finite complexity bounds. The zero-allowed theorem matches Dai et al.'s fixed-latent observational class when \(\mathcal I=\{\varnothing\}\) and extends it to joint interventions realized by one common mechanism and source tuple.

prose_updates.related_work: Dai et al. characterize observational distributional equivalence for the zero-allowed LiNG class; existing results do not characterize equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel sets or the additional requirement that one mechanism and source tuple realize all regimes. At \(\mathcal I=\{\varnothing\}\), the new zero-allowed theorem matches their fixed-latent observational class; for larger intervention families it adds simultaneous response constraints and common-mechanism gluing. The exact-support theorem remains the stratum-level engine, while the zero-allowed result is proved by the explicit finite union \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G)=\bigcup_{F\subseteq G}\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(F)\), not by a monotonicity assertion. Zhou et al. study do-calculus invariances for latent directed acyclic graphs rather than equality of cyclic parametric response-kernel sets. Bongers et al. supply intervention-solvability semantics. Hyttinen, Eberhardt, and Hoyer characterize experiment designs for second-order full recovery, and Taeb et al. study an acyclic Gaussian latent intervention setting; neither result eliminates unrestricted non-Gaussian source laws or certifies one joint latent feedback mechanism across regimes. Sharifian et al. provide a square no-latent row-recovery comparator, while the present source-partition, downward-closure, and common-response criteria address the graph-level latent cyclic law-set problem.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The population compiler is exact but intentionally exponential and uses deliberately loose real-algebraic bit bounds. It is uniform for each finite \(N\), fixed latent cardinality, and finite intervention family; it does not traverse unbounded latent cardinalities. The separate-versus-joint question still asks whether graph-generated regime-wise witness fibers can fail to share a common root and, if so, for a smallest explicit pair. The statistical theorem remains confined to the compact Laplace subclass with coefficient, inverse, edge, and scale margins.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved population results cover arbitrary independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources without centering or moment assumptions, arbitrary admissible algebraic cancellations, arbitrary cycles, exact support, and the zero-allowed downward closure on one fixed finite latent node set. The exact and zero-allowed criteria compare full affine response kernels under one common mechanism and source tuple; they do not claim source recovery from one observed law. Finite second moments are used only for the covariance formulation of the strict-refinement witness, and Laplace scales plus compact margins are used only for statistical certification. The new zero-allowed result matches Dai et al.'s fixed-latent observational class at the observational intervention family and supplies the additional common-mechanism joint-intervention constraints.

statement_notes.justification: The algebraic resolvent identity reduces every intervention kernel to an observational residual law and a finite response matrix without using means, centering, or moments.
statement_notes.gap: Published solvability semantics do not themselves give the principal-resolvent pushforward, source-visibility consequence, or the simultaneous representation used by the compiler.

statement_notes.gap: Dai et al. treat observational zero-allowed distributional equivalence, but the present theorem exposes the exact visible-column surjection, invisible columns, and irreversible merging needed inside the common-mechanism intervention criterion.
statement_notes.consumer: The population compilers enumerate finite source-partition types instead of optimizing over arbitrary probability laws.

statement_notes.gap: Dai et al. characterize the observational zero-allowed class, while existing latent intervention results do not characterize cyclic full-law response-kernel equality with shared source laws across all regimes.

proofs.proof_tex:
By Definition \texttt{def:witness-mechanisms}, an arbitrary mechanism on \(G_\star\) has equations
\[
L=\varepsilon_L,\quad
X_1=cL+aX_2+\varepsilon_1,\quad
X_2=bX_1+\varepsilon_2,\quad
X_3=dL+\varepsilon_3.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-support} gives \(a,b,c,d\ne0\).  Since \(\varnothing\in\mathcal I\), Assumption \texttt{ass:regime-solvability} applied to the observational regime gives
\[
\det(I-B)=1-ab\ne0.
\]
Define coefficients and sources for \(H_\star\) by
\[
\alpha=b^{-1},\quad
\beta=a^{-1},\quad
\gamma=-ca^{-1},\quad
\delta=d,
\]
and
\[
\eta_L=\varepsilon_L,\quad
\eta_1=-b^{-1}\varepsilon_2,\quad
\eta_2=-a^{-1}\varepsilon_1,\quad
\eta_3=\varepsilon_3.
\]
All divisions are licensed by \(ab\ne0\).  A permutation followed by nonzero coordinatewise scaling preserves mutual independence and nonconstancy.  It also preserves non-Gaussianity: if \(rW\) were Gaussian for \(r\ne0\), then \(W=r^{-1}(rW)\) would be Gaussian.  Thus the source restrictions in Definition \texttt{def:exact-support-model-class} are preserved without using centering or moments.

The same endogenous vector satisfies the resulting \(H_\star\) equations sample by sample.  Indeed,
\[
\alpha X_2+\eta_1
=b^{-1}(X_2-\varepsilon_2)
=X_1
\]
by the \(G_\star\) equation for \(X_2\), while
\[
\gamma L+\beta X_1+\eta_2
=-ca^{-1}L+a^{-1}(X_1-\varepsilon_1)
=X_2
\]
by the \(G_\star\) equation for \(X_1\).  Also \(L=\eta_L\) and \(X_3=\delta L+\eta_3\).  Consequently the two observational vectors agree almost surely under this coupling and have the same law.

The transformed mechanism has exact support \(H_\star\), because \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\ne0\).  Its feedback determinant is
\[
1-\alpha\beta
=1-\frac{1}{ab}
=\frac{ab-1}{ab}\ne0.
\]
For either witness graph and any observed intervention target \(S\), the only directed cycle remaining in the equations indexed by \(V\setminus S\) is the \(X_1,X_2\) two-cycle when \(S\cap\{X_1,X_2\}=\varnothing\).  Therefore
\[
\det(Q_{V\setminus S,V\setminus S})
=\begin{cases}
1-ab,&S\cap\{X_1,X_2\}=\varnothing\quad\text{for }G_\star,\\
1-\alpha\beta,&S\cap\{X_1,X_2\}=\varnothing\quad\text{for }H_\star,\\
1,&S\cap\{X_1,X_2\}\ne\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus every required intervention system is invertible, and no stability restriction has been used.

Conversely, let an arbitrary admissible \(H_\star\) mechanism have nonzero coefficients \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\) and mutually independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources \(\eta\).  Its observational solvability gives \(1-\alpha\beta\ne0\).  Set
\[
a=\beta^{-1},\qquad
b=\alpha^{-1},\qquad
c=-\gamma\beta^{-1},\qquad
d=\delta,
\]
and
\[
\varepsilon_L=\eta_L,\quad
\varepsilon_1=-\beta^{-1}\eta_2,\quad
\varepsilon_2=-\alpha^{-1}\eta_1,\quad
\varepsilon_3=\eta_3.
\]
Then \(a,b,c,d\ne0\), the source restrictions are preserved by the same argument, and
\[
1-ab
=1-\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}
=\frac{\alpha\beta-1}{\alpha\beta}\ne0.
\]
Direct substitution shows that this construction is inverse to the preceding one on coefficients and source laws.  Hence it is a bijection of the complete exact-support observational mechanism spaces.  Definition \texttt{def:graph-law-set} now yields
\[
\mathcal P_{\{\varnothing\}}(G_\star)
=\mathcal P_{\{\varnothing\}}(H_\star).
\]

It remains to distinguish the joint intervention classes.  By Assumption \texttt{ass:perfect-intervention}, \(\operatorname{do}(X_1=z)\) replaces only the equation for \(X_1\).  For an arbitrary \(G_\star\) mechanism, the remaining relevant equations are
\[
X_2=bz+\varepsilon_2,
\qquad
X_3=d\varepsilon_L+\varepsilon_3.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:source-independence} says that \(\varepsilon_2\) is independent of \((\varepsilon_L,\varepsilon_3)\).  Measurable transformations of independent random elements are independent, so \(X_2\) and \(X_3\) are independent in every such kernel.  This step uses neither centering nor moments.

For an arbitrary \(H_\star\) mechanism, write
\[
L=\eta_L,\quad
X_1=\alpha X_2+\eta_1,\quad
X_2=\gamma L+\beta X_1+\eta_2,\quad
X_3=\delta L+\eta_3.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-support} gives \(\gamma\delta\ne0\), and Assumption \texttt{ass:source-nondegeneracy} says that \(\eta_L\) is nonconstant.  Surgery at \(X_1=z\) gives
\[
X_2=\gamma\eta_L+\beta z+\eta_2,
\qquad
X_3=\delta\eta_L+\eta_3.
\]
Constants do not affect independence.  Apply Lemma \texttt{lem:single-shared-source-dependence} with
\[
U=\eta_L,\quad R_1=\eta_2,\quad R_2=\eta_3,\quad r=\gamma,\quad s=\delta.
\]
Its hypotheses follow from Assumptions \texttt{ass:source-independence}, \texttt{ass:source-nondegeneracy}, and \texttt{ass:exact-support}; hence \(X_2\) and \(X_3\) are dependent in every \(H_\star\) singleton-intervention kernel.

Independence of two coordinates is determined by their joint probability law.  Thus a \(G_\star\) kernel under \(\operatorname{do}(X_1=z)\) cannot equal an \(H_\star\) kernel under that intervention.  If \(\{X_1\}\in\mathcal I\), equality of two joint response-kernel tuples would imply equality of these singleton components, which is impossible.  Both graph model sets are nonempty: choose, for example, nonzero coefficients with feedback product different from one and mutually independent centered Laplace sources; the determinant calculation above verifies every observed intervention regime.  By Definitions \texttt{def:response-kernel-tuple} and \texttt{def:graph-law-set},
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G_\star)
\ne
\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H_\star)
\qquad\text{whenever }\{X_1\}\in\mathcal I.
\]

Finally, impose the finite-second-moment condition of Assumption \texttt{ass:source-second-moment} only for the covariance certificate.  Bilinearity of covariance and independence give, for \(G_\star\),
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(X_2,X_3)
=d\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_L)
+\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_3)
=0.
\]
For \(H_\star\), the same calculation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Cov}(X_2,X_3)
&=\gamma\delta\operatorname{Var}(\eta_L)
+\gamma\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_L,\eta_3)
+\delta\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_2,\eta_L)
+\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_2,\eta_3)\\
&=\gamma\delta\operatorname{Var}(\eta_L).
\end{aligned}
\]
Finite second moment and nonconstancy imply \(\operatorname{Var}(\eta_L)>0\), while exact support gives \(\gamma\delta\ne0\); therefore the last display is nonzero.  Under the inverse parametrization, \(\gamma=-c/a\), \(\delta=d\), and \(\eta_L=\varepsilon_L\), so it equals
\[
-\frac{c}{a}d\sigma_L^2\ne0.
\]
This proves the conditional covariance clause.  The identification argument uses no treatment overlap or positivity condition because it compares perfect-intervention population kernels at fixed \(z\); it uses no boundary or limiting argument.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(U,R_1,R_2\) be mutually independent real random variables, with \(U\) nonconstant, and let \(r,s\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\).  Then the two random variables \(rU+R_1\) and \(sU+R_2\) are not independent.  No moment or centering condition is required.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(\phi_U,\phi_1,\phi_2\) for the characteristic functions of \(U,R_1,R_2\).  Suppose, for contradiction, that
\[
Y=rU+R_1
\quad\text{and}\quad
Z=sU+R_2
\]
are independent.  Mutual independence of \(U,R_1,R_2\) gives, for all \(t,v\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[e^{i(tY+vZ)}\right]
=\phi_U(rt+sv)\phi_1(t)\phi_2(v).
\]
Independence of \(Y,Z\) gives for the same quantity
\[
\mathbb E[e^{itY}]\mathbb E[e^{ivZ}]
=\phi_U(rt)\phi_1(t)\phi_U(sv)\phi_2(v).
\]
We next verify directly that the two noise characteristic functions do not vanish near zero.  For \(j\in\{1,2\}\), choose \(K_j\ge1\) such that \(\Pr(|R_j|>K_j)<1/8\).  The elementary inequality \(|e^{iy}-1|\le |y|\), applied on \(\{|R_j|\le K_j\}\), and the bound \(|e^{iy}-1|\le2\), applied on its complement, give
\[
|\phi_j(t)-1|
\le \mathbb E[|e^{itR_j}-1|]
\le |t|K_j+2\Pr(|R_j|>K_j).
\]
Consequently \(|\phi_j(t)-1|<1/2\), and hence \(\phi_j(t)\ne0\), whenever \(|t|<1/(4K_j)\).  Put \(h_j=1/(4K_j)>0\).  Because \(r,s\ne0\),
\[
\rho=\min\{|r|h_1,|s|h_2\}>0.
\]
For \(|p|,|q|<\rho\), substitute \(t=p/r\) and \(v=q/s\) in the preceding identities and cancel the two nonzero noise characteristic functions.  This yields the local multiplicative equation
\[
\phi_U(p+q)=\phi_U(p)\phi_U(q).
\]
Taking \(q=-p\) and using \(\phi_U(-p)=\overline{\phi_U(p)}\), we obtain
\[
|\phi_U(p)|=1\quad (|p|<\rho).
\]

Let \(U'\) be an independent copy of \(U\).  Choose nonzero \(p,q\in(-\rho,\rho)\) with \(p/q\notin\mathbb Q\).  For either \(w\in\{p,q\}\),
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[e^{iw(U-U')}\right]
=\phi_U(w)\phi_U(-w)=1.
\]
The integrand has modulus one, so equality of its real-part expectation to one implies \(e^{iw(U-U')}=1\) almost surely.  Thus, almost surely,
\[
p(U-U')\in2\pi\mathbb Z
\quad\text{and}\quad
q(U-U')\in2\pi\mathbb Z.
\]
The irrationality of \(p/q\) forces \(U-U'=0\) almost surely.  If \(F_U\) is the distribution function of \(U\), independence of \(U,U'\) now implies, for every \(x\in\mathbb R\),
\[
0=\Pr(U\le x<U')=F_U(x)(1-F_U(x)).
\]
Hence \(F_U(x)\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(x\).  The limits and right-continuity of a distribution function then show that \(F_U\) is the distribution function of a point mass, contradicting that \(U\) is nonconstant.  Therefore \(Y\) and \(Z\) cannot be independent.
